kept.claim: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining, so any Google Meet booking whose event has no destination calendar (null/[]) throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar

**Severity:** HIGH — booking creation throws for Meet-location events without a destination calendar

### The Problem
```ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];
if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar") {
```
When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (handleNewBooking sets `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one) or `[]` (every other caller in this PR), destructuring yields `undefined`, and `.integration` throws.

### Theory / Proof
Array destructuring of an empty array yields `undefined` for the first binding (ECMAScript ArrayBindingPattern / iterator semantics). Property access on `undefined` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which safely returned `undefined` and triggered the Cal Video fallback — the exact scenario the comment above describes ("Google Meet is selected w/o a Google Cal").

### What happens today vs. what will break
Today (before PR) a user who selected Google Meet but has no destination calendar gets Cal Video. After this PR `EventManager.create` throws, and handleNewBooking's booking flow fails for those users — the precise case the fallback exists for.

### Research
Every other site in this PR (office365, lark, BaseCalendarService, BrokenIntegrationEmail) uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.…`; this one is the only one missing it.

### Recommendation
```ts
if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar") {
```
kept.evidence: EventManager.ts:117-119 dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining; handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets destinationCalendar to null when there is none, so Meet bookings throw TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video.

## [ISSUE] Video references lose credentialId, breaking meeting deletion on cancel

**Severity:** HIGH — cancelled bookings leave orphaned Zoom/Teams/etc. meetings

### The Problem
```ts
externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined,
credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined,
```
Before: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` — i.e. video results stored their own credential id. Now non-calendar results store `undefined`.

### Theory / Proof
`createMeeting` in `packages/core/videoClient.ts:78` sets `credentialId: credential.id` on the result specifically so the reference can be persisted. `handleCancelBooking.ts:490` only deletes the meeting `if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`; with `credentialId` null the `deleteMeeting` call is skipped.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Today (pre-PR) cancelling a booking with a Zoom location deletes the Zoom meeting. After this PR new bookings get a video reference with null credentialId, so cancellation silently leaves the meeting alive (and updates that key off the credential also degrade).

### Research
The sibling `updateLocation` code path in the same file keeps `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` for all result types — the create path should match.

### Recommendation
```ts
credentialId: result.credentialId,
```
(`createEvent` in CalendarManager now sets `credentialId` on calendar results, so no ternary is needed.)
kept.evidence: EventManager.ts:170 drops credentialId for video results; videoClient.ts:70,78 sets it; handleCancelBooking.ts:490-502 only deletes the meeting when credentialId is truthy, so video meetings are orphaned on cancel.

## [ISSUE] Unrelated change inverts organization slug logic

**Severity:** HIGH — orgs created without any slug when billing is disabled; paid flow bypassed when enabled

### The Problem
```ts
...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),
metadata: {
  ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {}),
```
Original: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The negation was dropped for the `slug` line.

### Theory / Proof
The design is: without billing, set `slug` directly; with billing, store `requestedSlug` and only promote it in `publish.handler.ts:54-68` after payment. Now with billing disabled, neither is set, and `createTeams.handler.ts:67` rejects with `!metadata?.requestedSlug && !organization?.slug`; `publish.handler.ts:54` also fails with "Can't publish organization without `requestedSlug`". With billing enabled the slug is claimed immediately, bypassing the payment gate.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Self-hosted / no-billing instances can no longer finish organization onboarding. This change is unrelated to the PR's destinationCalendar goal and is not mentioned in the description.

### Research
`update.handler.ts:82` and `publish.handler.ts` both assume the requestedSlug-only-when-billing contract.

### Recommendation
```ts
...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),
metadata: {
  ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {}),
```
or simply revert this file.
kept.evidence: create.handler.ts:151 lost the negation; with billing disabled neither slug nor requestedSlug is set, and createTeams.handler.ts:67 and publish.handler.ts:54-57 then reject; with billing enabled the slug skips the payment/publish flow.

kept.claim: Only Google's createEvent uses the new credentialId to pick its host's destination calendar; CalDAV/Apple (BaseCalendarService), Office365 and Lark always use destinationCalendar[0] (the main host's), so a second collective host on those providers gets their event filtered out or written to the wrong calendar id.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Multi-host destination only implemented for Google; other providers always use the first host's calendar

**Severity:** HIGH — the PR's fix does not work for non-Google hosts

### The Problem
`createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` once per host, and `CalendarManager.createEvent` passes `credential.id` to `calendar.createEvent`. But BaseCalendarService does:
```ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];
calendars.filter((c) => mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : true)
```
For host #2's CalDAV credential, none of their calendars match host #1's URL, so no event is created. Office365 (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73`) posts to `/me/calendars/<host1 id>/events` with host #2's token (404), and Lark does the same (`larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128`).

### Theory / Proof
Calendar ids are scoped to the account that owns them. Microsoft Graph returns `ErrorItemNotFound` for a calendar id not in `/me/calendars`; CalDAV calendar URLs are per-principal. Only Google's implementation resolves `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Collective events where every host uses Google work. Any host on Apple/CalDAV/Office365/Lark gets no event (BaseCalendarService silently creates nothing; O365/Lark error and are swallowed as failed results). The main host is unaffected, which hides the bug in single-provider testing.

### Research
Google's implementation in this same PR is the reference: it picks the destination matching the credential.

### Recommendation
Use the `externalId` that `createAllCalendarEvents` already knows, instead of index 0. E.g. in `CalendarManager.createEvent` pass a per-credential view:
```ts
const destination = calEvent.destinationCalendar?.find((c) => c.credentialId === credential.id);
const eventForCredential = { ...calEvent, destinationCalendar: destination ? [destination] : [] };
await calendar.createEvent(eventForCredential, credential.id)
```
so every provider's existing `[0]` logic becomes correct.
kept.evidence: Only googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:145-148 resolves the destination by credentialId; packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163, office365 :73-76 and lark :128-129 always use index 0. CalDAV returns success with no event written; O365/Lark errors are swallowed in CalendarManager.

kept.claim: In updateEvent (and deleteEvent) the fallback `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it can never match and the old fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is lost; update then calls events.update with calendarId undefined.

## [ISSUE] Google update/delete fallback is dead code; references without externalCalendarId break

**Severity:** MEDIUM — updates of bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId fail

### The Problem
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
The `find` branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is null/undefined/"", and then compares `cal.externalId === null` — always false, so `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`. Same pattern in `deleteEvent` (line ~315).

### Theory / Proof
Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. `calendar.events.update` requires `calendarId` (Google Calendar API v3 `events.update` path param); googleapis rejects a missing required param (`Missing required parameters: calendarId`). Also, this PR's `createAllCalendarEvents` else-branch (`destination` without credentialId) calls `createEvent(c, event)` without `externalId`, so new references in that path are stored with `externalCalendarId: undefined`, feeding this path.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Old bookings (created before externalCalendarId was stored) and new ones created via the no-credentialId path used to be updated in the destination calendar; now reschedule/location updates fail with an error. Delete falls back to `primary`, which 404s (swallowed) if the event lives in a non-primary calendar, leaving it undeleted.

### Research
Lark's version in this PR keeps a working fallback: `externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`.

### Recommendation
```ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId || "primary";
```
kept.evidence: googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:254-256 find() only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it can never match; events.update gets calendarId undefined. deleteEvent 315-317 falls back to 'primary'. References without externalCalendarId reach this path through EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents and the no-credentialId create branch.

kept.claim: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op and all other collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Team members' calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar

**Severity:** MEDIUM — collective hosts not invited in the exact scenario the PR targets

### The Problem
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar]
  : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null,
...
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);
}
```
Optional-chained `push` on `null` does nothing.

### Theory / Proof
The whole point of #7754 is that non-organizer collective hosts receive calendar events. Whether host #2 is invited now depends on whether host #1 happened to set a destination calendar. Moreover, with `destinationCalendar` null, `createAllCalendarEvents` takes the legacy else-branch and writes to *all* of the organizer's calendar credentials only.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Works when host #1 has a destination calendar; silently fails for host #2..N when host #1 doesn't.

### Research
All other callers in this PR default to `[]`, not `null`, which would have avoided this.

### Recommendation
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar]
  : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : [],
```
(and review whether an empty-but-team-populated array should still also hit the organizer's default calendars).
kept.evidence: handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets null; the optional-chained push at :1078 is a no-op, so the collected team calendars are discarded and createAllCalendarEvents falls into the organizer-only legacy branch.

kept.claim: For recurring bookings, the new per-reference loop re-runs the organizer-credential delete block once per calendar reference, and it only ever deletes each occurrence's first `_calendar` reference with the organizer's credentials, so other collective hosts' recurring events are never deleted.
kept.evidence: handleCancelBooking.ts:418-484: the recurring branch inside the per-reference loop uses only the organizer's credentials and the first _calendar reference of each updBooking; it runs N times and never deletes other hosts' references. Repeated deletes are swallowed on 404/410 (google CalendarService.ts:330-335).
